requirement:
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
rationale:
I found gaps in the `habeas author` path and in testing. The `habeas status` path and the validation obligations are implemented.

**Obligations:**
1. `habeas status` warns about every item without recent coverage, naming file, line, kind and name.
2. `habeas author` does the same after it finishes.
3. Items inside a module named `tests` are excluded.
4. A warning does not fail validation.
5. Repository validation does not read Git history.

**Implemented**
- **Status warnings:** `src/commands.rs#fn[status_markdown_with_github]` always ends by calling `coverage_warnings`. That calls `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[warnings]`, which filters out `in_tests` items, loads `RecentCoverage` from the evidence files on disk plus the last N commits (read through `git2`), and keeps only items not covered.
- **Message text:** The message comes from `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[uncovered_error]`, in the form `file:line: kind name has no recent coverage…`.
- **Tests-module exclusion:** `src/coverage_history.rs#fn[in_tests_module]` sets the `in_tests` flag in `src/rust_coverage.rs#fn[validate_rust_functions]`.
- **Validation:** `validate_rust_functions` puts uncovered items into `uncovered`, not into `errors`, so warnings do not fail validation. Only an untested `#[test]` becomes an error. `inspect_repository_with_progress` never calls `coverage_history`, so repository validation does not read Git history.

**Gaps**
1. **`habeas author` skips the warnings on one finishing path.**
   - `src/main.rs#fn[main]`, in the single-subject branch of `Command::Author`, returns early with `return Ok(());` after printing "evidence is current; 1 skipped as current (use --force to reassess)".
   - That return comes before `print_coverage_warnings(&root)`. The command has finished successfully but prints no warnings, so the "after it finishes" obligation is not met on this path.
   - The `--all` path and the normal single-subject path do print them. No test covers the skip path.
2. **Tests are weak on the stated format and the Git-history prohibition.**
   - The status and author tests in `tests/coverage.rs` check only that the text `function <name> has no recent coverage` appears. None asserts the file and line, which the requirement says each warning must name.
   - Nothing tests that repository validation does not read Git history. `coverage_lasts_for_three_reauthorings_of_the_record_that_read_an_item` checks only that `validate_repository` yields no error about `parse`.

The tests do cover:
- the `reauthored` window behaviour;
- `new_function`;
- the `test_module` exclusion;
- the incomplete-history note on a shallow clone;
- author's stderr output with `--all`.

Because of the author early-return path and the missing assertions, I judge the requirement not fully satisfied.

text: :::{req} coverage.report
`habeas status`, and `habeas author` after it finishes, MUST warn about every
item without recent coverage under
{cite}`requirements.references.coverage.history`, naming its file, line, kind,
and name, except items inside a module named `tests`. A warning MUST NOT fail
validation, and repository validation MUST NOT read Git history.
:::{req} coverage.history
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
:::{example} coverage.reauthored
Function `parse` has no reference, and the evidence of `requirements.cli.check`
read it. The requirement is re-authored and committed twice, and neither new
record reads `parse`. With the default window of 3, the record's third most
recent version still names `parse`, so `habeas status` does not warn. After a
third such commit, no version in the window names it, and `habeas status` warns
about `parse`. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.new_function
A new function `helper` has no reference, and no evidence record has ever read
it. `habeas status` warns about it at once; nothing in any window names it.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
:::{example} coverage.test_module
A helper function inside `mod tests` has no reference and is read by no record.
`habeas status` does not warn about it. A `#[test]` function in the same module
without a `{test}` reference is still a validation error.
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.report`
{test}`requirements.references.coverage.tests`
